what: On the smoke's second build the walk's summary query made 5.6 to 6.8 million `wait` spans on `summary_in` (one key changed owner 486,616 times) and the build did not finish in 600 s; with the call switched off the same daemon's builds had 954 and 27 such waits, longest 2.5 s.
cost: a build that never ends on any crate with mutually recursive functions (syn's `to_tokens`)
cause: a hint-only parallel pre-ask of callees' summaries, added 2026-11-11 in an uncompiled cut: an ask that would wait on its own asker gave way and ran again, with no bound. Its two test plants (`asking_in_turn`, `gathering_dry`) were called by no test.
whys: why a livelock: giving way and asking again is a retry loop, and a cycle of instances keeps every asker an owner's waiter
why unbounded: the hint was said to decide nothing, so nothing counted its rounds
why not caught: never compiled or run; no test called its plants
why written: single describes took 57 to 106 s on one worker; a fast path was bolted onto the walk in place of making the walk parallel by design
property: an optimisation whose failure mode is silent extra work
class: a fast path bolted onto the default (rule 66) with an unbounded give-way loop (rule 18)
prevention: removed whole: `ask_ahead`, `AHEAD`, `bounded`, `Walk::ahead` and its two gather sites, the plants; `summary_in` says why no pre-ask stands there
state: written on int-1112, not compiled or run by the lane
